differences.title: 1. PIPELINE ORIENTATION
differences.leftDesc: esbuild is designed around bundling and transform throughput: it parses once, builds a dependency graph, and emits JavaScript/CSS with tree-shaking and minification in one integrated pipeline.
differences.rightDesc: SWC is primarily a language tooling compiler: it focuses on fast AST transforms (TypeScript/JS/JSX/React) with configurable passes, typically integrated by higher-level bundlers.

differences.title: 2. PARSING/TRANSFORM HEURISTICS
differences.leftDesc: esbuild uses a pragmatic, performance-optimized parser and transformer, producing stable output quickly. Some edge-case semantics are handled via transform options rather than heavyweight compilation phases.
differences.rightDesc: SWC implements many transforms with AST fidelity aimed at spec-accurate behavior: it models syntax features and emits code according to plugin-driven transform semantics and target environments.

differences.title: 3. MINIFICATION STRATEGY
differences.leftDesc: esbuild’s minifier is tightly coupled to its bundler: it can rename symbols, drop unreachable code, and fold constants during emission, minimizing extra passes and memory overhead.
differences.rightDesc: SWC minification is usually achieved via dedicated minify-related transforms or toolchain integration; minification may be orchestrated as multiple AST/codegen stages.

differences.title: 4. PLUGIN ECOSYSTEM
differences.leftDesc: esbuild offers a straightforward plugin API around resolve/load and transform hooks, enabling bundler-like behaviors without forcing deep AST manipulation by default.
differences.rightDesc: SWC supports compiler plugins that can operate on the AST/codegen stages, enabling deeper, transform-level customization (e.g., syntax transforms) when orchestrated by surrounding tooling.

differences.title: 5. TYPE-SCRIPT HANDLING
differences.leftDesc: esbuild primarily strips TypeScript syntax and performs mostly syntax-level transforms. It targets fast compilation without full type-checking, relying on separate tooling for correctness.
differences.rightDesc: SWC focuses on fast compilation transforms for TypeScript syntax and can support additional transformations via plugins; it still typically avoids full type-checking, but richer passes exist.

differences.title: 6. TARGETING & OUTPUT CONTROL
differences.leftDesc: esbuild’s target options quickly determine syntax transforms and feature downleveling during bundling. Output control is direct and typically affects emitted code in a single integrated flow.
differences.rightDesc: SWC’s emit behavior is driven by compiler configuration and transform plugins, allowing fine-grained output customization. Code generation reflects the selected transform set and target settings.

differences.title: 7. RUNTIME PERFORMANCE PROFILE
differences.leftDesc: esbuild emphasizes low startup and low overhead: it can run extremely quickly for dev servers and CI, balancing minify/bundle features with tight CPU and memory usage.
differences.rightDesc: SWC leverages Rust for high-throughput AST transformation, often achieving strong parallel performance in toolchains that feed it many files and transforms concurrently.
